title: Seasonal harvest: transport, advances and freedom to leave
narrative:
This is an authored research scenario. The people, farm, records and amounts are fictional.

A seasonal fruit worker contacts an independent advice service from a packing shed during a break. The worker is an adult and has completed three weeks of a proposed eight-week season. A recruitment intermediary arranged transport, a shared room and an advance for ordinary family expenses. The worker confirms receiving the advance. Its repayment schedule is missing from the folder, while the employer's offer describes hourly pay and says nothing about the intermediary's debt.

The farm is several kilometres from the nearest town. A daily shuttle serves the accommodation and work site; there is no regular public bus. A photograph of a closed vehicle gate has prompted a friend to describe the worker as confined. The worker says the gate keeps livestock away from the road and has a pedestrian opening. That photograph alone says little about the worker's ability to leave employment. The latest messages below address the actual request to leave and transport choice.

Two wage deposits match the two payslips supplied. The worker controls the receiving account and has the original identity document. A deduction marked room contribution remains unexplained because the room invoice has a different weekly amount. The worker thinks one payslip may cover six nights rather than seven. An adviser could check the dates before deciding that either amount is wrong. The existence of an advance also leaves open who is collecting it and whether any proposed charge belongs to the worker.

A family care problem has made the worker consider ending the season early. The worker would also accept a shorter arrangement if it were a real choice and financially manageable. The farm manager has offered a different shift and says the crops will otherwise go unpicked. That staffing problem is part of the conversation, not a reason by itself to require continued work. The worker wants advice in a private call and has authorized no approach to the manager or intermediary.

[AG-R1] Worker account: "My wages reach my own account and I hold my original identity document."

[AG-R2] Supplied intermediary message: "You must keep working here until the advance is cleared. If you leave now, we will ask the farm to keep the pay still due."

[AG-R3] Supplied transport reply: "Your request to travel with the independent driver is refused. We will add a penalty if you arrange your own departure." The worker has enough money for that driver but fears the threatened loss.
user_question: I am the independent worker adviser taking this first call. Explain what the record supports about freedom to stop work, distinguish transport inconvenience from coercion, and suggest useful questions before any external contact. Which practical options could preserve the worker's wages and choice while the advance is checked?

Source publications retain their original populations and methods; this scenario supplies no industry prevalence estimate.
